title: Volume 1 Chapter 3: Pedicure 1
content: About a month had passed since I started doing Sayori Goto's nails. Sayori frequently came to the garage, wanting to repair her nails or try out new polishes. At first, I took a long time with the unfamiliar task, but I gradually got used to it, and now I could finish the necessary work in about an hour. Reducing the time spent on nail work was a good thing for Sayori, as staying in the same position for too long could be tiring.

I also decided to rearrange the garage a bit. The rugged, unadorned work desk now had a pastel-colored cloth draped over it, and I placed a few stylish lights around. The paint and glue stains that had stuck to the desk were hidden, making it look quite different. (I even prepared a place to sit…) I felt bad about using a folding chair all the time, so I borrowed an old sofa from home and asked my dad to bring it into the garage. With this, Sayori could sit comfortably for long periods while working.

I stored various tools like nippers in a drawer for now and set up the nail tools instead. There were cuticle removers and pushers for handling the cuticles, as well as base coats and top coats for before and after applying polish. Since Sayori's nails were efficient with a grinder, I probably wouldn’t need to use it, but I made sure to have various nail files on hand as well. I heard they were called buffers and shiners. With these tools standing by, the garage started to resemble a nail salon. (Speaking of which, she left some paint and magazines behind…) Although I took some of them back—most of the magazines and a large number of nail polishes Sayori brought were still left here. Since they belonged to Sayori, I made sure to store them properly. I bought a cheap magazine rack and placed it next to the sofa. It really felt like a waiting room at a salon. (…Well, I guess this is how it is.)

I could feel my once personal space, or secret base, in the garage being gradually taken over by Sayori. Surprisingly, I found that I didn’t mind it at all. I thought I liked being alone, but it seemed I didn’t mind company as much as I thought.
“Azuma-kun! I’m coming in!”
Just as I was thinking about that, Sayori arrived at my secret base. The monster—no, the dragon that had invaded my garage.
“Today, I want to change things up and have you paint this!”
Sayori showed me a polish she had just bought. This was the third time I was repainting her nails. She changed colors every ten days, but Sayori herself was in high spirits.
“Okay, okay. I’ll get ready now.”
When I said that, Sayori beamed and sat down on the sofa.
“Um, so… you have the UV curing machine for gel nails, right?”
“I do.”
“And you have an airbrush too?”
“Yeah, I have both a small one and a large one.”
“Then it’s basically a nail salon!”

We started the nail work while chatting about that. Throughout the process, Sayori’s chatter never stopped. Today’s topic seemed to be how there were commonalities between what modelers and nail artists used.
As I removed her old polish with the remover, I answered briefly. “My dad taught me a bit about that.”
“Eh? Your dad?”
“Yeah, according to him, nail polish was originally developed using techniques from automotive enamel paint. It was a fast-drying paint with great color that didn’t exist before.”
“Seriously!? Nail polish came from cars!?”
Nail polish isn’t exactly a car, but anyway, it seemed my dad had learned this as a fun fact.

“Plastic models used to mainly be car models and military models, so they were also derived from car painting techniques. In that sense, both plastic models and nails might have their origins in car paint…”
“You mentioned borrowing this garage from your dad, right? You work here?”
“Yeah. It’s off-limits on certain days.”
“Uh-huh. I get it♪ Nail salons have their days off too, right♪”
“It’s not a salon.”
I couldn’t deny that it was starting to look like one.
“I once watched my dad work, and I really like seeing how cars get painted smoothly and evenly.”
“Really~♪ Do you think I could watch if I asked?”
“I think it wouldn’t be a problem just to watch… but, well, it’s work, so I’m not sure.”
“Oh, if it’s not possible, I’m sorry!”
“Uh… well, I’ll ask you someday.”
“Okay.”

Sayori Goto was incredibly curious. It made me think there was nothing in this world that she wasn’t interested in or indifferent about. And I realized she never denied what others liked. She never had a negative comment about my model-making hobby or my dad’s work with cars. (No wonder she’s popular.) There were solid reasons for her being at the center of the class.
“So basically, cars, plastic models, and nails are all pretty much the same!”
“Don’t lump them together so carelessly…”

Having removed the old polish with the remover, I began the process of applying the new polish. (Still, it really is similar to painting models…) I proceeded with the work on Sayori’s now colorless nails. (First, surface treatment…)

First was shaping and surface treatment of the nails. However, since we had done this last time, it wasn’t necessary today. Shaping the parts and sanding the surface if needed was a process done in model-making too. The distortion (shrinkage) of the parts also affects the finish, so I checked it here. (Next is cleaning—)

I applied cuticle remover to her nails to soften the dead skin around the base. Since Sayori’s nails contained metal particles, human cuticle remover wouldn’t work, but it seemed to soften the surrounding cuticles properly. Next, I used a pusher to push back the cuticles and remove them. It was strange how her nails were unusually hard, yet the cuticles were about as soft as a human’s.
If I were to compare this to model-making, it would be the cleaning process of removing dust and plastic debris from the parts. (And then, the base coat—)

In model painting, there are three stages. First, you apply a primer called surfacer as a base. Apparently, there’s also a base coat for nails that serves the same purpose. (Then you apply the paint you want to color—)

After drying the base, I applied the main polish that Sayori wanted. This time, it was a light pastel pink polish. If I were to apply this to a model, I’d need to think about the color and apply it a bit thicker, but it seemed that polish worked differently, as it went on beautifully and evenly with just one coat. (Finally, the top coat)

Once the polish dried, I applied a finishing coat on top. The top coat had the same name in model-making, and it’s the paint applied last to protect the paint film. In other words, it’s a barrier for the paint film.

Even though the tools and paint contents were different, the order of processes in model painting and nail care was quite similar. Once I understood that, I found it easier to master. I quickly confirmed that it was dry before moving on to the next step.
“Giiiii—”
While I was doing that, Sayori turned her gaze toward me. In fact, she even said it out loud.
“Why are you staring so much?”
I asked while painting her nails, slightly distracted.
“Ehh~? Because you’re painting my nails with such a serious face, right? It makes me happy!”
“…Of course, I’m focused on the task.”
“Do you do the same when you’re working on models? That’s impressive.”
“Don’t look at me so much. I can’t concentrate.”
“Eh!? I don’t have anything else to do but look at you, Azuma-kun!?”
“Don’t move.”
I felt bad for Sayori, who pouted her lips, but being watched made it hard to concentrate.
Well, that might just be proof that I still had a long way to go—ideally, I should focus solely on the task at hand without being distracted by such things.
That said, it was unreasonable to expect me to concentrate when a popular beauty in class was staring at me. To avoid revealing my inner thoughts, I focused solely on her nails.
And today, in less than an hour, I completed the entire process from painting to drying her nails. (I’ve gotten quite fast.)
It was probably because I had done it so many times, but I could definitely feel my skills improving.
“Oh~! This looks great again! I’m so glad I asked you!”
Sayori beamed with a broad smile.
In the end, just painting her nails made Sayori happy, which made me feel good too.
Recently, our relationship had continued in this way, but—
As it progressed, another worry began to arise.
“Oh, good morning!”
When I entered the classroom, Sayori casually greeted me.
In her hand were the nails I had just painted yesterday. She waved her hand as she greeted me, so I had no choice but to respond.
“G-Good morning.”
“Mm!”
And just like that, Sayori returned to her conversation with the other girls.
Because the popular Sayori Goto was greeting me so friendly, the gazes of those around us felt piercing.
We had exchanged greetings before, but since I started doing her nails, the distance between us had clearly closed. The others must have sensed that too.
Why had the distance suddenly shrunk?
I could tell that the girls talking to Sayori and the other students were subtly questioning it. (This is unbearable…)

As an introvert, I really struggled with this kind of atmosphere. I wanted to avoid being the center of attention or being suspected of anything. I preferred to blend into the background as much as possible.
“Hey, Azuma…”
My seatmate, Miyabe, who had been watching the exchange with Sayori, spoke up awkwardly.
“Are you getting along with Goto lately?”
“Uh, yeah, well…”
What was I supposed to say?
Come to think of it—I recalled a conversation I had with Miyabe before.
“Right, um, we were talking about models. Model-making.”
Technically, it was a conversation about nails using model-making techniques, but I didn’t need to explain that much.
I still didn’t have the skills to say I could do nails well.
“I see—so you really were interested in models. I’m surprised, to be honest.”
“Because, um… it’s probably not what you guys are imagining.”
In other words, it wasn’t that a boy and girl suddenly became close or anything romantic.
It had nothing to do with that.
“Well, I’d be surprised if you said you started dating or something…”
“Exactly, that’s not it.”
“Got it. Just friends, then. Friends.”
Miyabe chuckled.
If there were suddenly a boy and girl getting closer in class, it wouldn’t be surprising for people to think that way.

But if I made excuses, it would only make it sound more “real.” I wondered how to handle that. However, in reality, my relationship with Sayori was not about romance at all. (It’s about nails, after all.)
It was purely a business-like relationship.
So I shouldn’t think about it. Forget about the rumors—
“Hey, Azuma-kun!”
Just as I was thinking that, Sayori closed the distance again.
“I have something I want to discuss, so can I have some time during lunch break?”
Her voice was loud.
